hook: Yann LeCun helped build the technique that underlies most of today's computer vision systems. He earned a PhD in computer science from Universite Pierre et Marie Curie in Paris in 1987, working on early ideas that fed into backpropagation based neural network training. At AT&T Bell Labs starting in 1988, he developed convolutional neural networks and built LeNet, a system for reading handwritten digits that was later deployed commercially to process a large share of checks handled by US banks. He went on to become a professor at New York University's Courant Institute, founding the NYU Center for Data Science, and in 2013 joined Facebook, later Meta, as founding director and then Chief AI Scientist of its AI research division. In 2018 he shared the ACM A.M. Turing Award with Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio for their work on deep learning. He left Meta in November 2025 after roughly twelve years to launch Advanced Machine Intelligence Labs, a venture focused on building AI systems around world models rather than only predicting text.

standing.watch: What comes next in the records is concentrated in the Meta litigation and in LeCun's new venture. The Kadrey plaintiffs are seeking interlocutory appeal certification after the June 2025 summary judgment for Meta on fair use, so that dispute remains unresolved. The New Mexico case has a penalties hearing set for October 1, 2026, where the state seeks up to $5,000 per violation after the jury found more than 43 million violations. Neural AI and Chicken Soup are both filed with docket monitoring active and no development recorded yet, leaving their course unknown. Advanced Machine Intelligence Labs is recorded as launched in November 2025 with a focus on world models, but the records supply no funding, valuation, listing plan, or product milestone for it. The site also lists Meta as a company where LeCun is an executive, while the profile says he left Meta in November 2025, a discrepancy the records do not resolve.
standing.record: The site's company record for LeCun contains one entry, Meta, described as a public company in Menlo Park, California, founded in 2004, with no funding or valuation figures supplied. The legal record contains four cases involving Meta: Neural AI, LLC v. Meta Platforms, Inc., Chicken Soup for the Soul, LLC v. Meta Platforms Inc., Kadrey v. Meta Platforms, Inc., and State of New Mexico ex rel. Torrez v. Meta Platforms, Inc. In Kadrey, summary judgment was granted for Meta on fair use in June 2025, and plaintiffs seek interlocutory appeal certification as of August 25, 2026. In the New Mexico case, a jury verdict for the state on September 25, 2026 found Facebook liable for deceiving users about privacy protections, with more than 43 million violations of the New Mexico Unfair Practices Act, and penalties to be set at a hearing on October 1, 2026, with the state seeking up to $5,000 per violation. The Neural AI and Chicken Soup cases are recorded as filed with docket monitoring active and no development recorded yet by this tracker. The pattern in these records is that LeCun's own profile is about research and institution building, while the litigation attached to him is entirely litigation against Meta, not against him personally.
standing.standing: Yann LeCun stands in the records as the executive chair of Advanced Machine Intelligence Labs and as the former chief AI scientist at Meta. The profile says he left Meta in November 2025 after roughly twelve years to launch Advanced Machine Intelligence Labs, a venture focused on AI systems built around world models rather than only predicting text. His technical standing rests on convolutional neural networks and LeNet, developed at AT&T Bell Labs starting in 1988, and on early work that fed into backpropagation based neural network training. He shared the 2018 ACM A.M. Turing Award with Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio, and he received the Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering in 2025. He also founded the NYU Center for Data Science in 2012 while a professor at NYU's Courant Institute. The site lists Meta as a company where he is an executive, while the profile records his departure from Meta in November 2025.

quick_facts: Developed convolutional neural networks and LeNet while at AT&T Bell Labs, a system used to read a large share of handwritten checks in the United States
Founded the NYU Center for Data Science in 2012 while a professor at NYU's Courant Institute
Served as founding director and later Chief AI Scientist of Meta's AI research division from 2013 to 2025
Shared the 2018 ACM A.M. Turing Award with Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio
Left Meta in November 2025 to launch Advanced Machine Intelligence Labs, focused on world models
Received the Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering in 2025

achievements.title: Convolutional neural networks and LeNet
achievements.impact: Created the architecture that underlies most modern computer vision systems and built an early commercial application that read handwritten checks.

achievements.title: NYU Center for Data Science
achievements.impact: Founded a research and teaching center in 2012 that helped establish data science as an academic discipline at New York University.

achievements.title: Chief AI Scientist, Meta
achievements.impact: Led Meta's AI research division for roughly twelve years, overseeing fundamental research including work on self-supervised learning.

achievements.title: 2018 ACM A.M. Turing Award
achievements.impact: Recognized, alongside Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio, for conceptual and engineering breakthroughs that made deep neural networks a critical component of computing.
